title: CAT 2024 Question Paper (Slot 3, QA) - Quant - Remainders
subject: Quant

questions.q: If $10^{68}$ is divided by 13 , the remainder is:
questions.explain: Using Fermat's Little Theorem, $a^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p}$. So, $10^{12} \equiv 1 \pmod{13}$. We can write $10^{68} = (10^{12})^5 \cdot 10^8$. The remainder is the same as $10^8 \pmod{13}$. $10^2 = 100 \equiv 9 \pmod{13}$, so $10^8 = (10^2)^4 \equiv 9^4 \pmod{13} \equiv (-4)^4 \pmod{13} \equiv 256 \pmod{13} \equiv 9 \pmod{13}$.
